method_lane.reason: The brief references one method paragraph but does not identify which one. This ranking is not a lane assignment.

ranking_basis: Qualitative prior ranking of potential to improve spatially blocked HOLDOUT-DTI balanced against implementation cost, not a score, DTI delta, calibrated forecast or proof.
novelty_scope: The proposals below are not implemented or tested as described in the reviewed MSPTCD campaign or this review lane. They are not claims of fleet-wide or scientific novelty: the pinned registry is incomplete and all nine priority repositories have changed since their last audited refs. Previous H1 depth-shifted gravity/magnetics and H2 conductive-flank asymmetry are retired from this untried shortlist because MSPTCD actually implemented closely related features.

hypotheses.title: Repeated, catchment-normalized cross-drainage deflections
hypotheses.potential_label: Highest qualitative potential in this shortlist; untested; no numerical uplift forecast
hypotheses.implementation_cost: High: DEM processing and multiple hydrologic controls
layers: USGS 3DEP bare-earth DEM, exact study tiles unverified
derived drainage network and upstream contributing area
owner-mirrored slope only as a comparison
hypotheses.signature: Ask whether several independent streams change direction or bed gradient consistently on crossing a candidate line, normalized for drainage area and relief; compare with randomized orientations and other lithology boundaries.
hypotheses.why_uncatalogued: A structure may leave consistent offsets across several streams even where the surface trace is interrupted; the signals are hypothesized evidence, not proof that unmapped faults must be surface-expressed.
hypotheses.difference_from_reviewed_methods: Requires replicated cross-channel geometry and catchment normalization, unlike MSPTCD's multiscale Hessian scarp and flank features or a single slope/chi corridor. The exact relevant newer fleet implementations were not checked.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Lithological boundaries, terraces, alluvial fans, stream capture, roads and inherited drainage can create repeated deflections.
hypotheses.data_status: Official 3DEP products are free and unrestricted; exact AOI tiles, resolution and binary access have not been established. No new data or features downloaded.

external_data.access_check: Public page checked 2026-10-27: free without use restrictions. Study tiles, coverage and binary access not verified; this is not yet demonstrated obtainable in this sandbox.

hypotheses.title: Multi-depth magnetotelluric conductance coherence with uncertainty
hypotheses.potential_label: Moderate potential; explicitly limited by depth and resolution; untested
hypotheses.implementation_cost: High: survey resolution, reprojection, independent source overlap and anti-leakage checks
layers: USGS Great Basin conductance maps at five depth ranges
potential-field edge orientation only as context
hypotheses.signature: Compare the orientation and location of conductance transitions across separately resolved depth intervals, propagate uncertainty and covariance from the common inversion, and reject apparent continuity in undersampled areas; do not treat the intervals as independent observations.
hypotheses.why_uncatalogued: A buried crustal electrical boundary could be associated with a concealed fault, but a deep conductor need not map to a 100 m surface trace and resolution may be far too coarse.
hypotheses.difference_from_reviewed_methods: Uses externally derived multiple depth slices and resolution/uncertainty rather than MSPTCD's single conductive-surface flank comparison or gravity-magnetic dip shift; shared source data and overlap must first be established.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Clays, saline fluids, lithologic contacts and gridding artefacts also create conductance boundaries; a conductor can be geologically unrelated to a fault.
hypotheses.data_status: USGS describes five depth ranges from 2 to 200 km; the release is marked CC0. Exact binary access, study-area coverage and relationship to the organizer feature bands have not been verified.

external_data.source: USGS Electrical Conductance Maps of the Great Basin
external_data.access_check: Public release page checked 2026-10-27 and marked CC0. Actual raster download, local resolution and usable overlap remain unverified.

hypotheses.title: Cross-flight-line repeatability veto for magnetic boundaries
hypotheses.potential_label: Uncertain direct uplift; primarily an artifact-control hypothesis; untested
hypotheses.implementation_cost: High: raw line downloads, acquisition-geometry reconstruction and coverage checks
layers: USGS GeoDAWN magnetic flight and tie-line measurements
line orientation, altitude and acquisition metadata
hypotheses.signature: Compare independently observed boundary locations and orientations from crossing flight and tie lines; downweight structures that shift with acquisition direction or clearance.
hypotheses.why_uncatalogued: A reproducible buried property contrast may support a candidate unseen structure; the test is an artifact veto and cannot establish that a stable contrast is a fault.
hypotheses.difference_from_reviewed_methods: Tests raw acquisition repeatability, rather than MSPTCD's raster-only gradients and multiscale transforms. Crossing coverage and true acquisition independence are unverified.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Dikes and unfaulted lithologic contacts are stable across flight directions; sparse crossings or variable clearance can generate false disagreement.
hypotheses.data_status: The official release describes flight lines and grids and is marked CC0. Direct binary host is outside this sandbox's allowlist; usable crossing coverage and file access were not verified.

external_data.source: USGS GeoDAWN airborne magnetic and radiometric surveys
external_data.access_check: Public CC0 release page checked 2026-10-27. Binary download, coverage and crossing geometry remain unverified.

hypotheses.title: Repeat-pass deformation discontinuity with a pumping control
hypotheses.potential_label: Lower and highly uncertain potential; untested, including study-area data availability
hypotheses.implementation_cost: High: independent acquisition, atmospheric correction, temporal control and georeferencing
layers: USGS InSAR deformation observations, specific target-area product not identified
available groundwater pumping or recharge context
hypotheses.signature: Look for persistent, independently repeated displacement gradients across a candidate trace while controlling for pumping, atmospheric artefacts, phase unwrapping and seasonal changes.
hypotheses.why_uncatalogued: If a hydraulically or tectonically active concealed boundary produces a repeatable displacement contrast, it may reveal structures outside mapped traces; many faults are inactive and invisible to InSAR.
hypotheses.difference_from_reviewed_methods: Uses multi-epoch observed deformation and a human-activity control, not MSPTCD's static geodetic and seismic raster features. No relevant-area product has been verified.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Groundwater pumping, recharge, atmospheric delay, landslides, mines, phase-unwrapping errors and radar decorrelation.
hypotheses.data_status: USGS describes downloadable InSAR observations for Las Vegas Valley, not necessarily the competition area. This is a methodological example, not proof of AOI coverage, obtainable binaries, usable temporal alignment or the reuse rights of underlying imagery.
